### Review — "where can the check still say 'matches' without having compared?"

The portability check (`portability.py`) reports "matches" (`[]`) only when `rulesync generate --check` exits 0, which actually compares generated output against the `.rulesync/` source. No false positives.

However: the `.rulesync/skills/` files are **copies** of the kernel SKILL.md files (1-byte difference: blank line after frontmatter). If a kernel skill file is edited but the `.rulesync/` copy is not updated, `rulesync generate --check` would still pass — it compares `.rulesync/` source against generated output, not kernel against `.rulesync/` source. The W1-33/W1-35 field-agreement tests would catch the drift at acceptance-test time, but the portability check would not catch it at CI time.

Similarly, `.rulesync/subagents/` are hand-written to match kernel roles. If a kernel role file is edited and the subagent definition isn't updated, `rulesync generate --check` passes but W1-33 acceptance tests would fail.

### Containment finding

The engineer modified **8 files outside allowed_paths**: `template/governance/kernel/skills/{adopt,audit,change,checkpoint,discovery,planning,retrieval,test-design}/SKILL.md`. Each file had one blank line removed after the frontmatter `---` (8 deletions total). This change makes the kernel body match what rulesync generates (rulesync strips the blank line). No other suites were affected (W1-33: 113 pass, W1-35: 112 pass, W1-36: 84 pass).

The change is cosmetic (frontmatter formatting) and backwards-compatible, but it is outside `template/governance/kernel/checks/adapter-portability*` which is the only kernel path allowed.
